messages.author: 49b995d6a750a593
messages.subject: Problem with .parallel in m_ply (plyr 1.2.1)
parts:
I encounter problem with m_ply in 1.2.1 version of plyr package.

Test data:

params <- data.frame(x=1:3, y=letters[1:3])
m_ply(params, .fun=function(x,y) {print(paste(x,y))})

Error in function (x, y) : unused argument(s) (.parallel = FALSE)
Calls: m_ply -> a_ply -> l_ply -> .fun -> do.call -> <Anonymous>

It seems that when m_ply call a_ply, which don't have .parallel
argument, then .parallel become part of ..., and then (in l_ply) is
treated as .fun argument (which isn't in above example).

As a workaround the function could have ... argument:
m_ply(params, .fun=function(x,y,...) {print(paste(x,y))})

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: Problem with .parallel in m_ply (plyr 1.2.1)
parts:
Hi Marek,

Oops, that was a mistake - I don't think *_ply should support
parallelisation, since parallelisation is chiefly useful for
collecting results, not for side effects. What are you trying to use
it for?

Hadley

messages.subject: Re: Problem with .parallel in m_ply (plyr 1.2.1)
parts:
My code perform some parametrized (so that's why m_ply) computation
(bootstrapping, etc.), write results to .csv and few plots to .png. I
don't need (for now ;)) this results returned to R so I used "no-
results" version.

Is parallelisation useful here? Could be, didn't consider it (since
it's new thing in plyr). I could always use mlply and return NULL from
each step to use .parallel argument.

messages.author: afa289b81aad98c2
messages.subject: Re: Problem with .parallel in m_ply (plyr 1.2.1)
parts:
Hi Hadley & Others... I think I have the same problem that Marek
reported, or something close (I get a warning, he got an error). The
warning message I get is

Warning in plot.xy(xy.coords(x, y), type = type, ...) :
".parallel" is not a graphical parameter

Which I believe is coming from this call:

cls.coords <- llply(ell, function(x) {x[1:2]})
cls.coords <- llply(cls.coords, function(x) {do.call(cbind, x)})
if (!use.sym) m_ply(cbind(x = cls.coords, col = gr$color, lty = 3),
lines, ...)
if (use.sym) m_ply(cbind(x = cls.coords, col = "black", lty = 3),
lines, ...)

Specifically, from the "lines" request (I could give full details if
needed). I think you are already on to this, but I thought I'd
mention it since the context is somewhat different than the one Marek
described.

Happy Holiday Season! Bryan
